requirements.text: placed under the Case Management support group

assumptions: no group named Case Management exists on the seed, so it must be created
id assumed next in sequence; the task creates one group
type support from the request's words 'support group'

requirements.text: Make sure she’s set up in the system and placed under the Case Management support group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 81 AND user_id = 4
assumptions: Joanne Simpson is user_id 4 (joanne.simpson@servicenow.com), already an active manager, so being set up means the group membership
id assumed next in sequence; the task creates one membership

requirements.text: the case is being assigned to Joanne Simpson ... the Case Management support group that’ll be handling this case moving forward
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 2 AND assignment_group_id = 81 AND assigned_to = 4
assumptions: assignment_group_id 81 is the new Case Management group
Joanne's role manager meets the policy's agent-or-manager rule for assigned_to, and the new membership makes her a member of the assigned group

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 2 AND state = 'pending'
assumptions: the policy marks a case pending once it is linked to a knowledge article; new to pending is a valid transition

notes:
Joanne Simpson already exists as user_id 4 (active, role manager), so no user row is created. 'She'll be focusing solely on this one' is not read as a removal of her existing memberships (CSM Tier 1 Support, Contract & Warranty Desk_4): the request asks only to place her in the new group and no listed tool removes a membership.
The benchmark's case check joins the assignment (asked by the request) and state pending (set by the policy once an article is linked); it is carried by two requirements, one per step.
The acting user Thomas Green (user_id 1) is an inactive agent on the seed; the policy's default is to act with admin responsibilities, so group and membership creation is treated as allowed, as the benchmark's checks assume.

disagreement: stay selector on case 2's links: one pass any article other than 197, the other the six FAS2750 Variant articles; chose the Variant articles because a stay marks the boundary a loose reading would cross, and the request does not forbid a further relevant link
